extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, Royal Society fellows, shipmasters and scientific observers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural recommendations for measuring, recording, and communicating magnetic-variation and related astronomical (sun amplitude/azimuth) observations at sea and on land; also includes experimental/laboratory procedure (phosphorus distillation), anatomical/dissection reporting, and data-quality requirements for mortality tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational coverage and reporting of magnetic variations
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘I must take leave to recommend to all masters of ships and all others, lovers of natural truths, that they use their utmost diligence to make, or procure to be made, observations of these variations in all parts of the world, as well in the north as south latitude, after the laudable custom of our East India Commanders, and that they please to communicate them to the Royal Society’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises wide geographic coverage (all parts of the world, both hemispheres), careful/diligent observation, following the East India Commanders' practice, and timely submission of observations to the Royal Society so future investigators can compare and test hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct method for measuring sun amplitudes / azimuths for variation observations
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It will not be amiss to correct a received error in the practice of observing the variation, which is, to take it by the amplitude of the rising and setting sun, when his centre appears in the visible horizon; whereas he ought to be observed when his under limb is still above the horizon about 4 of his diameter, or 20 minutes, on account of the refraction, and the height of the eye of the observer above the surface of the sea: or else the amplitudes are to be wrought as the azimuths, reckoning the sun's distance from the zenith 90° 36'’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the apparent centre-at-horizon time; instead observe when the sun's lower limb is still about 4' of arc (about 20 minutes) above the horizon, or compute amplitudes as azimuths using the correction 90°36' for sun's distance from zenith. This correction is minor near the equator but critical at high latitudes where oblique rising/setting causes large errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reliability and archival standard for observational records
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘All that we can hope to do, is to leave behind us observations that may be confided in, and to propose hypotheses, which after ages may examine, amend, or refute’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations should be trustworthy, carefully made and recorded so they can be relied on by future researchers; the primary contribution now is reliable data that later ages can use to test or revise theoretical hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distillation procedure for obtaining phosphorus from urine (critical steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: collect urine; distil with moderate heat until spirituous and saline parts are drawn off; evaporate remaining moisture to a thick syrup/ thin extract; incorporate with thrice its weight of fine white sand; place in a strong stone-retort joined to a large receiver partly filled with water, carefully luted; administer a gradual naked fire for 5–6 hours, then increase fire violently for another 5–6 hours — ‘which violence of fire is a circumstance not to be omitted in this operation’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the described sequence (gentle initial distillation to remove volatiles, then sustained violent heat). Use a strong stone retort and a water-filled receiver; careful luting is important. Observe the sequence of fumes (white fumes → faint bluish light → heavier substance) as indicators of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retort integrity and handling to produce solid phosphorus
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations: cracking of the retort before the operation is finished may prevent obtaining solid phosphorus; air or agitation of the receiver can cause liquid phosphorus to exhibit luminescence (‘I could in a dark place … perceive some glimmerings of light’)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure retort does not crack during the intense heating phase. Be aware that air contact or agitation in the receiver can kindle or affect the phosphorus product; controlling these factors influences whether liquid or solid phosphorus is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical construction methods for geometrical problems (temple dome quadrature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve by using relations between a triangle and a portion of a circle in the form of a lune (as determined by Hippocrates of Chios) and relations between circular spaces and the curved surfaces of spheres and cylinders (as demonstrated by Archimedes); use proportional arguments relating arcs, circumferences and diameters to cut off spherical surface portions equal to rectilinear figures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply classical results (Hippocrates' lunes, Archimedes' area relations) and proportional slicing of spherical surfaces by planes parallel to the base to convert curved surfaces into equivalent rectilinear areas; multiple methods can be offered for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic observation and reporting of ‘animalcules’ (Leuwenhoek-style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine reproductive organs and spawn under magnification; report morphology (shape, size), numbers (e.g., '10,000 of them equal not one thread'), and the medium they occur in (transparent oily liquor, thread-like vessels); compare with prior observations and infer modes of generation (egg vs carried young)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed morphological descriptions, quantify abundances where possible, compare with similar observations (eels in vinegar, etc.), and cautiously infer origins/generation methods based on observed structures (e.g., presence of eggs vs embryonic development in the parent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for anatomical dissection reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe external and internal anatomy in detail, compare to related species (e.g., rat fore-feet like castor), note presence/absence of organs (gall-bladder absent, only ductus felleus), relative sizes and positions (testicles in groins on os pubis), and provide labelled figures (e.g., fig. 1 with A A kidneys; aa renes succenturiati; etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparative anatomy, morphological detail, precise anatomical terminology, and labelled illustrations to support observations; record unusual features and measurements where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data requirements and population criteria for mortality tables / annuity estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of prior uses of Bills of Mortality: defects included missing total population counts, lack of ages of the deceased, and distortion from migration/visitors. Prefer data from locations where people die where born and without adventitious immigration/ emigration. Example: Breslaw tables provided monthly ages and sexes of deaths compared to births over multiple years (1687–1691) and executed with exactness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sound deduction about mortality and pricing annuities, use mortality tables that record ages and sexes of deaths, include the number of people, cover multiple years for stability, and ideally represent a stable, non-migratory population to avoid bias from migration or transient visitors.
